record.paper_title: The variance of departure processes: puzzling behavior and open problems
record.original_question: What are the proper minimal assumptions on the inter-arrival-time and service-time distributions under which the critically loaded GI/G/1/K queue satisfies the conjectured BRAVO asymptotic γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K)? In particular, which tail or moment conditions are actually needed, since the paper's exponential-moment light-tail assumption appears stronger than necessary and the author does not know the correct minimal condition.

evidence.quote: We are thus quite confident that the exponential moments condition of our conjecture is too strong, yet we are not sure what the minimal condition is.
Proper (minimal) conditions on the inter-arrival and service time distributions are yet to be determined.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a single-server queue with finite buffer of size K (a GI/G/1/K queue): customers arrive according to a renewal process with i.i.d. inter-arrival times having mean 1/λ and squared coefficient of variation c_a^2; service times are i.i.d., independent of the arrivals, with mean 1/μ and squared coefficient of variation c_s^2. Customers arriving to a full system (K customers present, including the one in service) are lost. The queue is taken to be critically loaded, meaning λ = μ. Let D(t) denote the number of service completions (departures) in [0, t] in steady state, and define the asymptotic variance rate

   V_K := lim_{t → ∞} Var(D(t)) / t,

and the normalized quantity γ*_K := V_K / (the corresponding service rate). The BRAVO (Balancing Reduces Asymptotic Variance of Output) conjecture for this model asserts that, as K → ∞,

   γ*_K = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K).

This conjecture has been formulated under the assumption that the inter-arrival and service distributions possess finite exponential moments (light-tail condition). Determine the minimal moment / tail conditions on the inter-arrival and service-time distributions under which the above asymptotic formula γ*_K = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) holds. In particular, identify a sharp moment hypothesis (e.g., a finite p-th moment for some specific p) replacing the exponential-moment assumption.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2022–2024) on BRAVO for critical GI/G/1 and GI/G/1/K queues has progressively weakened moment assumptions—e.g., establishing busy-period regular variation under finite second moments and reducing the uniform-integrability hypothesis from fourth to lower moments—but a sharp minimal-condition characterization for the γ* = (1/3)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) + O(1/K) asymptotic in GI/G/1/K is not reported as established. The problem of identifying the proper minimal tail/moment condition appears still open.

status_evidence.title: On busy periods of the critical GI/G/1 queue and BRAVO
status_evidence.snippet: A key technical component for a complete proof of GI/G/1 BRAVO is uniform integrability, which was previously established only under the simplifying assumption that fourth moments are finite.
status_evidence.claim: Moment assumptions for BRAVO have been progressively reduced but a sharp minimal condition is not yet known.

status_evidence.title: Phase transitions and departure statistics of critically loaded queues
status_evidence.snippet: The cumulants of the departure statistics deviate strongly from Poissonian values and oscillate in the vicinity of phase transitions, i.e., if a critical load is approached.
status_evidence.claim: The behavior of departure variance for critically loaded finite-buffer queues continues to be an active research topic.

status_evidence.title: The asymptotic variance of departures in critically loaded queues
status_evidence.snippet: For critically loaded GI/G/1 queues the asymptotic variance rate equals λ(1−2/π)(c_a^2 + c_s^2) under specific moment assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: The classical BRAVO result is established under stronger-than-necessary moment hypotheses.
